page: Amazon Web Services i2.xlarge is a legacy storage-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. The CPU features 25 MB of shared L3 cache and supports AVX and AES-NI instruction sets, though it lacks modern vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX. The instance includes 30.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.62 GB per core.

A central characteristic of the i2.xlarge is its bundled local storage subsystem, featuring 800 GB of direct-attached solid-state storage. There are no discrete hardware accelerators included. Network throughput operates at a baseline of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned to the instance by default.

Benchmark results highlight the limitations of this older hardware generation compared to modern compute platforms. PassMark CPU scores reach 4485.27, with multi-core stress-ng performance measuring at 3619.57 and Geekbench 6 multi-core scoring 1136.0, placing overall computational capacity in the lower quartile of modern evaluation suites. Memory throughput records 26.24 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 16.45 GB/sec for writes. Redis operations yield 1.53 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 4.13 GB/sec.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the instance pairs a substantial 800 GB local SSD and 30.0 GB memory capacity with comparatively lower compute density. It remains suited primarily for legacy database engines, transactional datastores, and batch workloads that rely on dedicated local NVMe-equivalent SSD scratch space without demanding high-throughput modern CPU performance.
description: Amazon Web Services i2.xlarge is a second-generation storage-optimized instance operating on the Xen hypervisor. Equipped with an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, the configuration delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores alongside 30.0 GB of memory. It features 800 GB of bundled local SSD storage and a baseline network capacity of 1 Gbps, with zero integrated GPUs. Synthetic evaluation demonstrates dated processing performance, registering a PassMark CPU score of 4485.27 and multi-core stress-ng throughput of 3619.57. Memory transfer speeds achieve 26.24 GB/sec on uncached reads. Given its moderate compute power coupled with direct-attached high-capacity SSD storage, this instance is suited for legacy database workloads, caching layers, and local scratch processing needing fast disk access over heavy compute.
